name: Jordan Lee
summary: Product data analyst with seven years in analytics, the last four and a half in product analytics for a B2B SaaS payroll and time-tracking company whose customers have 5 to 200 employees. I build the churn model and account health score that Customer Success works from, and I run A/B tests with the product team. Every quarter I present a retention review to the VP of Product.

bullets: Built the Python churn model (pandas, scikit-learn) that scores all 38,000 active accounts every night and flags those likely to cancel within 60 days. In a held-out quarter, about 42% of the model's top 200 accounts cancelled, against a 6% base churn rate. Customer Success calls the top 200 each month.
Built the account health score for Customer Success from weighted product-usage signals. It is refreshed daily by an Airflow job and shown in Tableau.
Fitted a Cox survival model for the churn work, then mentored a junior analyst on survival analysis and reviewed her extension of the model to add-on accounts.
Reviewed about five GitHub pull requests a week from the team's two other analysts.

Analysed retention for the time-tracking add-on. Of the add-on accounts that connected their scheduling tool in week one, 81% were retained at 90 days, against 63% of those that did not. A new onboarding checklist was built to push that step.

Designed and ran the checklist's A/B test with the onboarding product manager and an engineer. Sized it with a power calculation to detect a 4-point lift in week-one activation, the decision metric. About 4,000 new accounts were split 50/50 over six weeks, and the variant raised activation from 41% to 47%.
Ran two smaller A/B tests on the pricing page. Neither showed a clear difference.
For the 2024 pricing review, analysed seat expansion among accounts that added the time-tracking add-on.
Presented churn drivers to the CEO, CFO and VP of Product at the 2024 planning offsite. The time-tracking add-on's pricing was changed afterwards.
Built a Snowflake and Airflow data pipeline that replaced the finance team's hand-updated spreadsheets with scheduled SQL transformations. Wrote a data dictionary for the 60 core Snowflake tables.
Worked out the Segment event tracking for new features with product managers before launch.
Automated the weekly loan-pipeline report with SQL and Power BI. Preparation time fell from about six hours to under one.
